title: Product contribution and margin calculator
description: Separate sales revenue, variable cost, contribution and gross margin before deciding what an order can support.
formula: Price minus product cost gives gross profit. Subtract packing and the entered payment fee to estimate contribution. This is not net profit: fixed costs, taxes, refunds and owner costs not entered remain excluded.
example: At ₹1,000 with ₹600 product cost, ₹50 packing and a 2% fee, gross margin is 40% and contribution is ₹330.
limit: Do not compare this result with another product whose cost boundary excludes different items.

title: Target contribution price calculator
description: Estimate the selling price required for a chosen rupee contribution when a percentage payment fee applies.
formula: Required price = (variable cost + desired contribution) ÷ (1 − fee rate). The model assumes the fee applies to this price only. It is not a tax or provider-fee calculation.
example: With ₹500 cost, ₹150 target and 3% fee, the unrounded result is about ₹670.1031; rounding up to ₹670.11 keeps the target within this model.
limit: A desired contribution is a planning choice, not evidence that buyers will accept the resulting price.

title: Break-even order planner
description: Find how many consistent orders would cover a stated fixed-cost budget.
formula: Break-even orders = fixed costs ÷ contribution per order, rounded up to the next whole order. Use a contribution figure after the variable costs you intend to include.
example: ₹12,500 divided by ₹300 requires 42 whole orders; 41 provides ₹12,300 and leaves a ₹200 gap.
limit: This simplified model assumes a stable order mix and does not forecast demand or cash timing.

title: Discount ceiling calculator
description: Estimate the largest discount that still leaves your chosen contribution after variable cost and a percentage fee.
formula: First find the required retained price: (cost + target) ÷ (1 − fee rate). Compare it with the current selling price. If the required price is higher, there is no feasible discount in this model.
example: At ₹1,000, ₹600 cost, ₹150 minimum contribution and 2% fee, the retained price must be at least ₹765.31 when rounded up to paise.
limit: Shipping subsidies, other discounts and provider-specific fee bases can reduce the real ceiling. Enter a complete cost boundary.

title: Bundle contribution calculator
description: Test a proposed bundle price against its component costs, packaging and fees.
formula: Contribution = bundle price − total component cost − packing − percentage fee. Enter the total component cost, not the average cost of one item.
example: A ₹750 bundle containing ₹540 of components and ₹30 packing contributes ₹180 before excluded costs.
limit: This does not prove that the bundle improves sales or uses stock better than selling the components separately.

title: Free-shipping threshold planner
description: Estimate a basket value that could fund a delivery subsidy and retain a chosen contribution.
formula: Threshold = (delivery subsidy + desired retained contribution) ÷ pre-delivery contribution rate. The rate must already account for the variable costs other than this subsidy.
example: An ₹80 subsidy plus ₹100 retained contribution at a 40% rate gives ₹450.
limit: The result is not a promise that every basket qualifies economically. Low-margin product mixes, remote-area charges and returns need separate checks.

title: Acquisition spending limit planner
description: Set a scenario budget from expected qualifying orders, contribution and the amount you want to retain.
formula: Maximum scenario spend = qualifying orders × (contribution before acquisition − retained contribution). A negative result means the retention target is not feasible before any campaign spend.
example: Twenty qualifying orders at ₹300 contribution, retaining ₹100 each, leave a ₹4,000 scenario spending allowance.
limit: Expected orders are your assumption, not a prediction. Reconcile actual cancellations, refunds and spend before deciding to continue.

title: Monthly versus annual plan comparison
description: Compare the cash cost of monthly billing with an annual commitment over a chosen usage period.
formula: Monthly scenario cost = monthly charge × months. Compare it with the full annual upfront payment. No refund, cancellation credit, tax or renewal offer is assumed.
example: At ₹1,200 monthly and ₹12,000 annually, six months cost ₹7,200 monthly; a full year costs ₹14,400 monthly, ₹2,400 more than the annual commitment.
limit: Lower annual unit cost does not mean a smaller immediate cash commitment or a better choice for uncertain use.

title: Made-to-order capacity planner
description: Estimate available production slots after reserving time for administration and rework.
formula: Available production hours = total hours − reserved hours. Whole-item capacity = available hours ÷ hours per item, rounded down.
example: Forty available hours, ten reserved and three hours per item give ten production slots.
limit: This is a time model, not an inventory or delivery promise. Drying, supplier delays and concurrent tasks may require a separate schedule.

title: Reorder-point worksheet
description: Estimate a stock trigger using your own daily demand, replenishment lead time and safety allowance.
formula: Reorder point = daily usage × lead time + safety allowance, rounded up to a whole unit. Compare with usable stock and outstanding replenishment deliberately.
example: Three units per day over seven days plus five safety units gives a trigger of 26 units.
limit: Historical averages can hide seasonality and unreliable lead times. This worksheet does not place a purchase order or synchronise stock.

title: Store launch budget planner
description: Separate one-time launch spending from recurring costs and an explicit contingency.
formula: Planning total = setup + assets + monthly cost × months + contingency. Keep stock purchases and advertising outside the result unless you deliberately include them in the entered categories.
example: ₹15,000 setup + ₹5,000 assets + twelve months at ₹1,500 + ₹3,000 reserve gives ₹41,000.
limit: A budget is not a vendor quotation. Check taxes, renewals, scope exclusions and whether costs are due upfront or later.

title: Product photography session planner
description: Estimate capture workload and write a local shot list without uploading product or customer data.
formula: Required shots = products × views. Planned session minutes = shots × minutes per view + setup. Editing, retakes and travel are excluded unless added to your time estimate.
example: Twelve products with four views each give 48 shots; three minutes each plus one hour setup gives 204 minutes.
limit: The calculator counts planned views, not usable finished images. Inspect focus, accurate colour and product identity before treating the session as complete.
